clue.text: Obsession — by the sound of it, a grisly thing inspiring fear

explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' nods to the word itself, which sounds like a grisly bear (a grizzly); the second sense is the old goblin of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent worry or pet hate, and in folklore a goblin used to scare children.

clue.text: City where ammunition is stored, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: a bomb bay is the compartment in an aircraft that holds bombs

explanation.surface: A city with a munitions dump, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian port, now officially Mumbai, is a major metropolis.

clue.text: Girl — one taking shelter in the porch

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A girl sheltering from the weather in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the porch' is the definition: the term is used for a porch or chapel at a church entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: In church architecture, the term names an entrance chapel or vestibule at the west end, as at Durham Cathedral.

clue.text: Where list was compiled formerly

indicators.note: compiled means put together, so these letters are assembled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about where a list was drawn up in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an old-fashioned word for previously, at an earlier time.

clue.text: Providence here has no riddle to be solved

indicators.note: a riddle to be solved is worked out, so these letters must be rearranged

explanation.surface: God's plan here contains no mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Providence' looks like divine guidance, but it is the US state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of this smallest US state.

clue.text: Work it out, keeping information to oneself — that's best

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: out signals that the little word it is muddled or worked out into a new order

parts.note: keeping mum means saying nothing, keeping something secret

explanation.surface: Advice to solve a problem privately because silence is the wisest course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal on 'it' alone, giving TI; 'Work it out' reads as one instruction to solve something.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum is the most favourable or ideal condition, the very finest.

clue.text: Number that is 1/3 of 9

indicators.note: a third of the nine-letter answer means only its final three letters are kept

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer of 9 Across, a landmark event

explanation.surface: An arithmetic puzzle about the fraction of a number.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' is not the number nine but the answer to 9 Across; its final third is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest positive whole number, a numeral.

clue.text: Where to find the brave finally put to the sword

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word put

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A grim scene where a courageous warrior is at last executed by the blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but is a Native American warrior; 'finally' applies to 'put', not 'brave'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped tent of the Plains peoples, home to a warrior.

clue.text: Make up mother used to conceal a blemish

indicators.note: the mother word is used to hide the next pieces inside it

parts.note: ma is mother
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Mum puts on cosmetics to hide a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used to conceal' is the container signal; 'Make up' is the definition, meaning cosmetics, not invent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a cosmetic for darkening eyelashes.

clue.text: Criminal had up in connection with horse

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the run of letters is written from bottom to top

parts.note: re means concerning, in connection with
Red Rum was a famous British racehorse, three times winner of the Grand National steeplechase

explanation.surface: A villain arrested over a matter involving a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RE plus REDRUM (the horse Red Rum) as one run; 'had up' reads as arrested, but 'had' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer is a criminal who has taken a life.

clue.text: It's of historical importance, in case nothing is found in the excavation

indicators.note: found in tells us the next two pieces sit inside the dug-out word that follows

parts.note: a mine is an excavation dug for coal or ore
lest means in case, for fear that
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An archaeologist hopes nothing turns up empty in the dig, just in case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' places the in-case word and the zero inside the dug pit; the definition is the opening phrase, a significant event.
explanation.definitionFit: A landmark event marks a significant stage in history, like a roadside stone marking distance.

clue.text: A problem for a model

definitions.meaning: a puzzling question or tricky conundrum
someone who sits or stands for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: A tricky puzzle is a teaser, and a person striking attitudes for a camera holds a pose.

clue.text: Own everything? Own most of it

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: most of means the second 'Own' loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether to possess the lot or just the greater share.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Own' is the definition, in its sense of admit or concede; the second is trimmed to OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To own a fact is to concede or admit it, the same as granting it is true.

clue.text: Clear out of 5dn with speed

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
5dn points to the answer of 5 Down, a number
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear out of somewhere quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate someone is to free them from blame, declaring them innocent.

clue.text: Riotously drank, looted, knocked 'em here

indicators.note: riotously means wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Rowdy looters got drunk and caused havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked 'em in the Old Kent Road' is a music-hall song; the street is in south-east London, the cheapest square on a British Monopoly board.
explanation.definitionFit: The south London street is where, in the old music-hall song, the singer wowed the crowds.

clue.text: He argues against addict, evolves a different way

indicators.note: arranged a different way means these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A drug user develops along another path in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different way' rearranges ADDICT EVOLVES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking the opposing side for argument's sake, originally the Church official arguing against canonisation.

clue.text: Under one's control, like a kite

definitions.meaning: a kite flies tethered by a line held by the flyer

explanation.definitionFit: A puppet controlled by its handler is tied to a cord, just as a flying kite is.

clue.text: Boy's head with girl's kerchief

indicators.note: the head of the word Boy's is its first letter

parts.note: and means with, as in fish and chips
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A boy's head wrapped in a girl's scarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large patterned handkerchief worn round the head or neck.

clue.text: Each seat's wobbly, perhaps, according to circumstances

indicators.note: a wobbly thing is unstable, so the letters of these words are shaken up

parts.note: read as 'seats', the plural, giving its letters
maybe means perhaps

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that all the chairs in a room are unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' rearranges EACH SEATS into ASTHECASE; then add MAYBE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means depending on how things turn out in a given situation.

clue.text: Silk got damaged going round foreign warship

indicators.note: going round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: tore means ripped, got damaged
USS (United States Ship) prefixes American naval vessels

explanation.surface: Fabric torn while wrapped around an overseas naval vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal: the ripped word surrounds the American ship prefix.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse brown silk from wild silkworms, also spelt tussah.

clue.text: Top of branch burning here

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word branch

parts.note: burning means alight, in flames

explanation.surface: The tip of a tree limb is blazing in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a heap of branches set alight outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor blaze of wood and garden waste, where branches burn.

clue.text: Wrong trap set up for this game

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so the whole run is reversed

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: An unfair snare devised for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' sounds like a frame-up, but reverses SINNET.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: Cast doubt on record, having soundly understood it

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: soundly here means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: 'read it' means understood it, as in reading a situation; said out loud it gives the second half

explanation.surface: Someone queries a recorded document after taking it in properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals the sound of 'read it' (red it).
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to throw suspicion on it, making it seem unbelievable.

clue.text: One given to charging cash

definitions.meaning: an animal known for rushing at threats, horn first

explanation.definitionFit: The horned African beast is famous for charging, and rhino is dated British slang for money.

clue.text: Exciting present, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the present is one example of a grammatical verb form, alongside past and future

explanation.definitionFit: A thriller can be nerve-racking, and past, present and future are the grammatical time forms of a verb.

clue.text: I complain about girl

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: moan means complain

explanation.surface: A man grumbles about a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but reverses IMOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a female given name, from the Old Testament mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Supply food for six — the number is rounded

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: rounded here means turned round, so the two words before it are read backwards

explanation.surface: A caterer feeding six people mentions that the head count is approximate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounded' sounds like approximation but reverses NOIS to SION.
explanation.definitionFit: To provision a party or ship is to stock it with food and supplies.

clue.text: Small coin that is (or was) worth little in India

definitions.text: Small coin that is (or was) worth little in India

parts.note: P stands for penny, a small British coin
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A tiny coin that has little value in India, now or in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The pie was the smallest copper coin of British India, a twelfth of an anna.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-value copper coin formerly used in India, worth a fraction of an anna.

clue.text: Bloomer made by a submariner knew no bounds

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

indicators.note: with no bounds means the word knew loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gaffe committed by a sailor on a submarine who acted without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant. 'knew' without its outer letters is NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blooms is a flower, and the windflower is a spring-flowering plant.

clue.text: Line up without a soldier who's about to stray

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the line-up word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to dress ranks is to line soldiers up straight

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier out of formation is about to wander off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses GI to IG; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the line-up word goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the main subject of a talk or text.
